extra.message: Sensitive internal operations gated only by static shared token — If the static INTERNAL_OPS_TOKEN leaks (logs, source, misconfig) an attacker gets unauthenticated access to command execution, arbitrary file write, and PII disclosure [verified: _wrk_gate is the sole control on all /ops routes, a single static header compared with !=, gating RCE/file-write/PII endpoints.]

Static shared token as sole authentication for high-privilege /ops endpoints — Single leaked/guessed static token grants command execution, arbitrary file write, and PII disclosure across all ops routes [verified: _wrk_gate uses non-constant-time != comparison against a static env token as the sole gate for RCE/file-write/PII endpoints.]

Server-side template injection via dynamic Jinja template construction — Arbitrary code execution on the server via Jinja2 sandbox escape payloads [verified: fragment is concatenated into the Jinja template source string before compilation, allowing SSTI/RCE payloads.]

OS command injection via ping host parameter — Arbitrary OS command execution on the server as the app user [verified: host is concatenated raw into os.system's shell string with no sanitization, enabling shell metacharacter injection.]

Cross-tenant ticket status update via integration API key (missing tenant scoping) — A partner integration (or a leaked/rotated key from one org) can modify (close, resolve, reopen) any customer's support tickets across all tenants, causing SLA/data integrity damage and cross-tenant business logic abuse. [verified: update_ticket_status_from_api loads any Ticket by ID (integrations.py:72) and calls transition_ticket with no organization/tenant scoping check, unlike create_ticket_from_api which validates requester.organization_id == org.id; ApiKey has no tenant binding either (app/deps.py api_key_auth just authenticates the key).]

Hardcoded default admin credentials and API key created by seed script — Anyone who reads the source (or knows this is a common seed script) obtains a working support_admin login and a valid API key for any deployment where the seed script has been executed, granting full administrative access and partner-API access to ticket/org data. [verified: seed.py unconditionally creates a real support_admin user (admin@supportdesk.local) with hardcoded password DEMO_PASSWORD and a hardcoded API key DEMO_API_KEY, with no environment/production guard, and prints both to stdout in main().]

Sensitive data (SSN/partner token) exposed in ops response — Disclosure of SSN and live partner sync token to anyone possessing the static ops header value [verified: endpoint returns a live-looking sync token and SSN-shaped tax_ref in plaintext, gated only by the weak static token.]

Path traversal in ops vault stash endpoint — Arbitrary file write to attacker-chosen path, and stores plaintext SSN/card data at rest [verified: ref from query/body is inserted unsanitized into the file path and also causes plaintext SSN/card persistence.]

Sensitive data (SSN/card number) exposed and stored in plaintext — Disclosure and plaintext persistence of PII/PCI data (SSNs, card numbers), regulatory and fraud risk [verified: SSN/card accepted from request JSON are echoed back and written unencrypted via write_text, plus hardcoded token/SSN returned elsewhere.]

Path traversal in ops file dock endpoint — Arbitrary file write outside the intended export directory, potentially overwriting server files or planting web shells [verified: name is joined directly into BASE_EXPORT_DIR with no traversal check and written via write_bytes.]

NoSQL injection via unrestricted Mongo filter passthrough — Query logic bypass / broad data exfiltration from the ops Mongo collection [verified: payload.get('filter', payload) is passed directly as the Mongo query document to find_one with no validation.]

Hardcoded default admin credentials exposed in login UI — Any unauthenticated visitor can read the default admin email/password straight from the client bundle and log in as support_admin if the seeded account/password was never rotated, granting full administrative control over tenants, users, and integration API keys. [verified: app/seed.py creates a real admin@supportdesk.local account with password DemoPass!2026, and main.jsx pre-fills and displays these credentials to any anonymous visitor with no forced rotation, letting anyone log in as support_admin if the seed data persists in deployment.]

Potential path traversal in SPA static fallback route — Arbitrary file disclosure from the server filesystem if traversal segments reach the handler [verified: file_path = frontend_dist / path uses the raw path parameter with no normalization or containment check (no .resolve()+is_relative_to guard), so a path containing '../' segments can escape frontend_dist and FileResponse will serve arbitrary readable files.]

Mass assignment allows overwriting privileged fields — Attacker-controlled request can set is_admin/role/credit_limit fields that a real caller of this workset data might trust [verified: arbitrary client JSON is merged via dict.update into workset including is_admin/role, then returned unrestricted.]

Open redirect via lane parameter — Phishing / credential-theft redirects hosted on a trusted domain [verified: lane is used unchecked as the RedirectResponse target with no allow-list or same-origin check.]

Sensitive data (bearer token) written to logs — Session/API bearer tokens leak into log files, which may be less protected than the primary datastore [verified: raw body and Authorization bearer header are logged verbatim at warning level with no redaction.]

Sensitive bearer token and request body logged in plaintext — Credential/token leakage to log storage, enabling session/account takeover by anyone with log access [verified: duplicate of finding 10 — logger.warning logs raw body and bearer header verbatim.]

Reflected XSS via unsafe Jinja template rendering — Arbitrary script execution in the context of a user viewing the rendered page (stored/reflected XSS) [verified: card is rendered via Template with |safe, disabling escaping and allowing arbitrary HTML/JS injection.]

CORS misconfiguration reflecting Origin with credentials allowed — Any malicious website can make authenticated cross-origin requests and read responses, enabling session/data theft [verified: Origin header is reflected verbatim as ACAO while ACAC is true, allowing any origin credentialed access.]

Privilege escalation via trivially forgeable cookie/header check — Attacker sets a cookie/header to obtain elevated data disclosure (payroll/casework) without any real authorization [verified: ops_badge cookie/header equality to 'lead' is the entire check with no server-side signature verification.]

CSV formula injection in ticket/SLA report exports — Attacker-controlled ticket subject/description containing a spreadsheet formula executes when a staff member opens the exported CSV, potentially exfiltrating data from or compromising the staff member's workstation (client-side RCE via legacy DDE, or data exfiltration via web-request formulas). [verified: csv_response writes rows via csv.DictWriter with no escaping of leading =/+/-/@ characters, and ticket.subject/description are attacker-controlled free text exported verbatim (reports.py:52, tickets.py:92) to staff who open the CSV; this is a real CSV/formula injection risk though impact is limited to client-side spreadsheet apps.]

Use of broken MD5 hash — Hash collisions/predictability could be leveraged wherever this digest is trusted as a unique or tamper-evident identifier [verified: MD5 is used to hash phrase into a returned digest, a broken/weak algorithm for any security-relevant identifier.]

Security headers disabled (CSP cleared, XSS protection disabled) — Weakens defense-in-depth against XSS/clickjacking for this endpoint's responses [verified: endpoint explicitly empties CSP and sets X-XSS-Protection to 0, removing browser mitigations.]

Security headers explicitly disabled — Weakens browser-side mitigations against XSS/clickjacking for responses using this pattern [verified: duplicate of finding 13 — same header-clearing code disabling XSS protections/CSP.]

Weak PRNG used for security-sensitive code generation — Predictable tokens/codes could be brute-forced or guessed by an attacker [verified: random.choice (Mersenne Twister) generates the returned code instead of secrets/os.urandom, making it predictable.]
